text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV said on Friday net profit for the first nine months of 1996 rose 16.6 percent to 1.10 billion guilders ($651.4 million) from 0.94 billion in the same period of 1995, slightly better than analysts had forecast.
Net profits per share rose by 15.6 percent to 4.15 guilders.
The firm raised its 1996 earnings forecast slightly, saying it expected full-year net profit and net profit per share to increase in line with the nine-months figures.
In August Aegon said earnings and earnings per share for the whole of 1996 would rise by 15.7 percent and 15.0 percent, respectively.

Aegon chairman Kees Storm said he was particularly pleased that life insurance and pension premium income had shown healthy growth in all group units helping the company to improve its market position.
Life insurance and pension premium income increased by 26.6 percent in the first nine months of 1996 to 9.51 billion guilders, representing 76 percent of the group's total premium income.
The life insurance sector counted for just over 80 percent of pre-tax profits
"Focusing primarily on life insurance and pensions, Aegon is clearly well positioned to benefit from the opportunities for further growth in this market worldwide," Aegon said.

Aegon said it had realised a significant increase in non-life earnings in the Netherlands, especially in motor and fire insurance, but accident and health results were depressed by further strengthening of claims reserves.
In the United States the growth in results was fuelled by the strong increase in sales of pension plans and variable universal life products.

The contribution to Aegon's pre-tax profits from Scottish Equitable rose by almost 55 percent to 96 million guilders. Aegon raised its stake in Scottish Equitable to 80 percent from 60 percent at the end of 1995.
Shares in Aegon were down one guilder at 93.80 half an hour after the release of the nine-months figures.
